summary: Iteration 5 fully validated. Backend (8/8 new tests + regression pass): GET /api/ndis-catalogue returns full catalogue (version=2024-25.1, last_updated=2024-07-01, source_note, items[] with code/name/category/subcategory/unit/rate/icon/tags — 25 items). GET /api/ndis-catalogue/version returns version+last_updated only. GET /api/ndis-codes returns 25-entry list with code/label/rate/unit. GET /api/clients/{id}/recent-codes correctly returns de-duplicated codes from last 3 invoices, most-recent-first. Verified with 3 invoices (inv1: 01_011+0812, inv2: 01_011+04_104, inv3: 07_002) → returns [07_002, 04_104, 01_011, 0812] in that order with description+rate. Also verified: empty client → [], 4-invoice test proves oldest invoice's UNIQUE code (15_054) is correctly excluded (only last 3 considered). Invoice regression: POST /api/invoices computes subtotal=270.24/gst=27.02/total=297.26 for 4×67.56; PUT edit recomputes 357.60/35.76/393.36 for 5×67.56 + 20×0.99. Frontend (390x844): /ndis-codes screen loads offline-first bundled catalogue immediately (loadCatalogue()), version pill shows 'v2024-25.1 · 2024-07-01', search 'sunday' filters correctly (weekday hidden), tag 'Transport' shows 0812 only, Add button on code 01_011 navigates to /invoice/new?presetCode=...&presetRate=... and pre-fills ndis-code-btn-0 with '01_011_0107_1_1' + item-rate-0='67.56'. /invoice/new picker: link-client-btn → pick-client-{id} sets clientId which triggers api.clientRecentCodes → 'RECENT FOR THIS CLIENT' section appears at top of picker modal with the 3 recent codes (04_104, 0812, 01_011) each with description + $67.56/$0.99/$67.56 rates; code-search 'travel' filters to 0812, codetag-Sunday chip filters to sunday code; tapping recent-code-04_104_0125_6_1 applies code + rate to line item. Only harmless RN-web warnings (shadow*/pointerEvents deprecations + expo-notifications web limitation) — no pageerrors.

minor.issue: Uses invoice created_at descending sort AND limit(3) at DB level. If a user later back-dates an invoice with issue_date (edit), created_at ordering will not reflect the true chronological order the user perceives on the invoice list. Consider sorting by issue_date DESC (fallback created_at) for consistency with the invoices list UI.

Returns items in insertion order of the seen-dict which is 'first occurrence wins' scanning newest→oldest — this correctly gives most-recent-first for de-dup, but the endpoint response omits any 'last_used' timestamp making it hard for the UI to show 'used 3 days ago'. Nice-to-have.

Now returns all 25 catalogue items instead of the previous 10-item hard-coded NDIS_CODES list (server.py lines 183-194 is DEAD CODE — the NDIS_CODES module-level constant is defined but never used). Recommend removing the unused NDIS_CODES list to avoid confusion.

issues: Category section headers (styles.sectionHeader) show right on top of the ListHeaderComponent 'source_note' italic paragraph — spacing looks fine but the source note may be missed as a footnote. Consider a subtle info banner.

When tags are toggled OR search text is present, RECENT FOR THIS CLIENT section is hidden (`recentCodes.length > 0 && !codeQuery && codeTags.length === 0`). This is intentional but users may be confused when they type into search that their recent codes disappeared. Consider keeping the section visible when only search is applied.

'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents.' Non-blocking. Carried from prior iterations.

action_items: (Optional cleanup) Remove the dead NDIS_CODES module-level list in /app/backend/server.py (lines 183-194) — it is no longer referenced now that /api/ndis-codes reads from CATALOGUE_ITEMS.
(Optional UX) In /invoice/new picker modal, keep 'RECENT FOR THIS CLIENT' visible when only search-text is applied (filter within recents too) so users don't lose the shortcut when they start typing.
(Optional) Add a 'last_used' ISO date to each recent-code entry so the UI can display 'used 3 days ago' or a subtle chip.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py loads /app/backend/ndis_catalogue.json once at startup into CATALOGUE_ITEMS — good, no disk hit per request. Version endpoint returns only {version,last_updated} which is a light payload perfect for the client-side version-check.

/api/clients/{id}/recent-codes uses `.sort('created_at',-1).to_list(3)` which returns at most the last 3 invoices for the client, then walks items in that order de-duping by ndis_code with a dict (Python 3.7+ preserves insertion order). Correctly returns [{code, description, rate}] most-recent-first.

frontend/src/ndis.ts loadCatalogue() implements true offline-first: bundled JSON → AsyncStorage cache (if newer) → backend fetch (if newer). Sets updateAvailable when the online version is newer than the bundled but not yet stored. Clean design.
frontend/app/ndis-codes.tsx uses SectionList with groupByCategory + FILTER_TAGS chips + query search. Add button correctly router.push('/invoice/new', { presetCode, presetDesc, presetRate }).

frontend/app/invoice/new.tsx wires useEffect on clientId → api.clientRecentCodes(clientId). Recent codes list only shown when !codeQuery && codeTags.length === 0 to avoid overlapping with active filters. applyCode() reuses the item's own description if already populated, otherwise falls back to code.name — good UX.

InvoiceCreate PUT preserves shift_id/recurring/recurrence only when 'not update.get(x)' — this can still clobber non-default values (e.g. explicitly setting recurring=False in edit form would fall into `not update.get(...)` and re-inherit the previous True). Carried from iter-4.
server.py still has bson.ObjectId() calls without try/except across most endpoints — malformed 24-hex IDs still return 500 not 400. Non-blocking, carried from prior iterations.
